message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — 44 shares at a $222.90 limit (filled at $222.90, ~$9,808).**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and the fundamentals support a modest addition: total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — with gross margin improving to 46.2% (from 44.1%) on Services strength ($96.2B, +13%, at 73.9% margin) and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Net income and EPS dipped slightly versus FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) mainly because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%), which is non-recurring rather than an operating deterioration; the company also returned $95.0B via buybacks and $15.2B in dividends. Risks I noted are real but not disqualifying: Greater China net sales fell 8% to $67.0B, iPhone sales were flat, and there is ongoing antitrust/regulatory exposure (DOJ suit, EU DMA proceedings with fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales). The quote was $222.70 last (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so my $222.90 limit was within ~0.1% of market. The order complies with the mandate: AAPL is permitted, it is a buy, the ~$9,808 notional is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap (no other orders today), and it was funded from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account. I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares.
